newsitem.title: UK: Vardon says expects better 2nd half results.
newsitem.headline: Vardon says expects better 2nd half results.

text.p: An overall strong economy triggering higher consumer spending is expected to boost the second half performance of UK's leisure and entertainment clubs group Vardon Plc, the company said on Wednesday.
In a statement, the company said trading in the second half had exceeded its expectations so far with a strong performance from the health and fitness division.
"Our other divisions have also benefited from the general economic recovery and improvement in consumer confidence," Vardon said.
The company's share price gained 6 1/2 pence at 89p in trade turnover of 92,600 shares at 0940 GMT.
The company is due to announce its results for the year ended December 31 1996 on February 26, 1997.
Vardon's pre-tax profit in 1995 was 9.14 million stg on a turnover of 52.6 million.
Vardon's newly acquired health and fitness division has continued to perform ahead of expectations.
"Trading has been strong at the nine metropolitan clubs with membership income increasing by 22 percent for far this year.
Its bingo sales remained strong with revenue increasing by four percent. "...Like for like club admissions in the five months ended November 30 are in line with 1995...", the company said.
The holiday division at Parkdean Holiday Parks reported a 17 percent hike in revenue for five months to November 30, 1996 when compared year-on-year.
The company said its net borrowings at the year end is expected to be less than 35 million stg with a level gearing of 43 percent. It has medium term bank facilities of 45 million stg.
